blogs.title: The Art of Letting Go: Shaping Irregular Forms
blogs.author: Monami Chakraborthy
blogs.excerpt: In this week's studio notes, we explore the beauty of imperfection. Moving away from symmetrical perfection allows the natural character of the raw material to shape the final form.
content: For years, I thought precision was the goal. Every line had to match. Every shape had to be controlled. But the more I worked with clay, wood, and paint, the more I noticed that perfection can sometimes erase personality.
Irregular forms have a pulse. They carry the trace of the hand that made them. Slight asymmetry, a soft edge, or an unexpected curve often holds more emotion than a flawless finish.
This week, I intentionally stepped away from strict outlines. I let the material suggest the next move. The result felt more alive. Less designed. More honest.
If you are creating something right now, try leaving one part unresolved for a little longer. You might discover a shape that feels more true than the one you planned.

blogs.title: Observations from the Autumn Woods
blogs.author: Monami Chakraborthy
blogs.excerpt: Collecting fallen leaves, sketching textures, and finding profound inspiration in the quiet color shifts of the season.
content: Autumn reminds me to pay attention to transitions. Colors do not change overnight, they drift into one another. That gradual shift is a design lesson in itself.
I spent a few mornings collecting textures: cracked bark, dry stems, and leaves that looked hand-painted by weather. These references are now guiding a new set of surface experiments.
Nature does not repeat exact patterns, and that is exactly what makes it rich. I am bringing more of that uneven rhythm into upcoming collections.

blogs.title: The Morning Light Mug Collection
blogs.author: Monami Chakraborthy
blogs.excerpt: Introducing our latest batch of hand-thrown mugs, designed to make your slow mornings feel warmer and a little more personal.
content: This collection started with a simple question: what shape feels right at 7 AM? We tested handle curves, rim thickness, and weight distribution until each mug felt easy to hold in a sleepy hand.
The glaze palette stays grounded: warm neutrals, charcoal accents, and one soft blush variation. Enough variety to choose your mood, but still cohesive as a family.
Every piece is made in small batches, so slight variation is part of the story. No two mugs are exactly alike, and that is the point.
